intended_object: For a subset s ⊆ M, the R-submodule of the monoid algebra S[M] made of the elements whose support (the set of m with nonzero coefficient) lies in s. Taken from the docstring.
explanation:
The definition pulls back `Finsupp.supported S R s` along the R-linear equivalence `coeffLinearEquiv R : S[M] ≃ₗ[R] (M →₀ S)`. `Finsupp.supported` is the submodule of finitely supported functions whose support lies in s, so x lies in the new submodule exactly when its coefficient function is supported in s. The library's lemma `mem_supported` (`x ∈ supported R S s ↔ ↑x.coeff.support ⊆ s`, proved by `.rfl`) confirms this.

The generality is the natural one. R and S are arbitrary semirings with `Module R S`, M is an arbitrary type, and s is an arbitrary set. In the degenerate cases it gives the expected answers: s = ∅ gives the zero submodule, and s = univ gives the whole algebra.

`Finsupp.supported` is the same construction for `M →₀ S`. `MonoidAlgebra` is a separate structure wrapping such functions, so transporting the notion along the coefficient equivalence is the right way to make it available on S[M]. It does not restrict generality.
